drhp.business: The Company is in the business of hospitality, food products and allied activities, running a chain of restaurants serving hygienic standardised food items in a quick-serve format at outlets on national highways, state highways and in cities. Its business model is to develop the operating systems and grant franchises under trade marks to restaurant chains operating in dine-in and kiosk formats; the Company does not own the brands 'Vithal Kamats', 'Kamats' and others and has licensed them from their respective owners. risks.note: MD&A: 'As the industry remains closely linked to discretionary consumer spending, any adverse economic developments may impact demand and operating performance.' Hotel and restaurant volumes therefore swing with the consumption cycle rather than with contracted demand.
risks.risk: Demand is tied to discretionary consumer spending

risks.note: MD&A Threats, Risks and concerns explicitly names 'inflationary pressures, rising manpower, utility and food costs'. These are the dominant operating costs of a restaurant and hotel chain and are hard to pass on quickly in a value/mid-market format.
risks.risk: Input-cost inflation - manpower, utilities and food

risks.note: Flagged in the MD&A risk paragraph. The Company's formats are standardised quick-serve, themed dhaba, multi-cuisine and premium South Indian dining; a shift in dining preference directly affects footfall across the licensed brand portfolio.

Named in the MD&A risk paragraph; the same MD&A notes the restaurant segment is expanding on organised dining, premiumisation and technology-enabled delivery platforms, i.e. the industry is drawing in competition and new channels.
risks.risk: Rising competitive intensity in hospitality and organised dining

risks.note: MD&A names 'regulatory changes' as a risk, and the year's key policy development was the 56th GST Council rationalisation effective 22 September 2025 (5% GST without ITC on room tariffs up to Rs.7,500/day). The Secretarial Audit also lists the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 as laws specifically applicable to the Company.
risks.risk: Regulatory change, including tax and food-safety regulation

risks.note: MD&A: 'The Company is presently operational in only one segment i.e. hospitality, food products and allied activities.' There is no diversifying business line to offset a hospitality downturn.

The Board's Report states 'Profit before tax was registered low due to initial operating cost of new outlets.' Two projects are still to land - the Urban Dhaba (Urban Bar) restaurant at Bhandup expected to commence by July 2026 and the subsidiary's ~100-room Nani Daman hotel targeted for the coming financial year - so near-term earnings carry start-up drag and completion risk.
risks.risk: Execution and ramp-up risk on new outlets and hotel projects

risks.note: The Board's Report describes the Kamats Hospitality Academy of Skill (KHAS) as an initiative 'to address the concern of skilled labour', i.e. management itself identifies skilled-manpower scarcity as a constraint on a business it also calls manpower-dependent (171 employees on the payroll as on 31 March 2026).

sk.overview: The overnight ocean and coastal cruise industry in India is a nascent, high-growth segment of cruise tourism.
